plz.title: Postcode & premium region
plz.oneLiner: Sets your premium region — premiums differ by municipality, not just by canton.
plz.short: Your premium depends on where you live. Many cantons are split into two or three premium regions, and the region that applies is determined by the municipality, not the postcode alone. If a postcode covers several municipalities, you pick yours.

birthYear.title: Birth year & age group
birthYear.short: Premiums differ across three age groups: children (0–18), young adults (19–25), and adults (26+). Your birth year sets your age group, and with it the deductible tiers available to you.

franchise.title: Deductible (Franchise)
franchise.oneLiner: A higher deductible lowers your monthly premium.
franchise.short: The deductible is the share of your medical costs you pay yourself each year before the insurer starts paying. Adults choose between CHF 300 and CHF 2500. A high deductible means a lower premium but more out-of-pocket risk if you need care. The coverage is identical either way.

unfalldeckung.title: Accident coverage
unfalldeckung.short: Basic insurance normally also covers accidents. If you're employed at least 8 hours a week by an employer, you're covered for accidents through them and can exclude accident coverage from your health insurer — which lowers the premium slightly. If unsure, leave it included.

models.title: Insurance models
models.short: In the standard model you see any doctor you choose. Alternative models (family doctor, HMO, Telmed) require you to contact a set first point of care for health questions — your family doctor, a health centre, or a phone advice line. In exchange the premium is lower. The scope of coverage stays the same.

guide.lead: Basic insurance (OKP) is mandatory and, by law, identical at every insurer. So you're only comparing price, model, and service — not the scope of coverage.

rules.heading: The rules everyone follows
rules.item1: Basic insurance is mandatory. After you move to Switzerland you have three months to take out cover — it applies retroactively to your arrival date.
rules.item2: Every insurer must accept you for basic insurance. There are no health questions and no rejections.
rules.item3: You can switch insurer once a year. Your cancellation must reach your current insurer by 30 November; the switch takes effect on 1 January.
rules.item4: The scope of coverage is set by law and is the same everywhere. A cheaper insurer is not less insurance.

models.heading: Standard or alternative model
models.body: In the standard model you choose your doctor freely. Alternative models (family doctor, HMO, Telmed) lower your premium; in exchange you contact a set first point of care for health questions. The coverage is the same.
